title: When successful requests return bad data
scenario: Customers report strange or missing delivery estimates and shipping prices. Monitoring still shows successful requests. Find out whether the shop can trust the information it receives.
why: A fast HTTP 200 response can still contain unusable data. Protect customers from incorrect delivery promises while keeping stock visible.
reproduce: Record healthy stock and shipping first, then predict the impact. In Network Faults, apply Invalid shipping responses under Shipping response faults. Refresh shipping several times and investigate. The fault stays active until you remove it.
assignment: Can you prevent incorrect quotes from reaching customers without hiding healthy stock?

fields.label: Healthy baseline and prediction
fields.prompt: Record normal stock, delivery days and shipping price. Predict what an unusable response could affect.

fields.label: Storefront and Grafana evidence
fields.prompt: Record examples from several refreshes. Compare HTTP outcomes with invalid and rejected quotes.

fields.label: Diagnosis and uncertainty
fields.prompt: What explains successful requests with incorrect customer information? Name an alternative explanation.

fields.label: Protection and reason
fields.prompt: Which control did you apply? Explain why timeout, fallback or breaker alone does not validate successful responses.

fields.label: Validation under the same fault
fields.prompt: Keep the fault active. Record whether incorrect values are blocked, stock remains live and rejected quotes increase.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: What did customers regain, what is still unavailable, and what must the carrier fix? Remove the fault and verify normal quotes return.

solution: Primary Shipping returns HTTP 200 but cycles through negative delivery days, empty fields, a negative price and a valid quote. Stock remains healthy.
HTTP success stays high while Shipping data quality records invalid quotes. A successful request is not proof that its contents are usable.

Enable Validate shipping quotes and apply validation. Missing fields, negative prices and non-positive or non-integer delivery days are rejected. The shop shows unavailable quote information while retaining stock.

Validation is independent of fallback and breaker. It does not repair the carrier or automatically request a backup quote. Keep the fault active to verify protection, then remove it and restore defaults.

text.hints_description: Open one at a time if you get stuck.

hints.title: Hint 1 · Compare the symptoms
hints.explanation: Refresh shipping several times. Compare stock, delivery days and shipping price. Does the HTTP status explain everything customers see?

hints.title: Hint 2 · Look beyond HTTP success
hints.explanation: Compare Dependency outcomes with Shipping data quality in Grafana. Invalid quotes are measured even when protection is off. Rates use a one-minute window.

hints.title: Hint 3 · Choose the right protection
hints.explanation: Timeout limits waiting and breaker reacts to failed calls. Neither checks the contents of a successful response. Look for a separate quote-validation control. It blocks invalid data without switching carriers.
